name: sre

findings.message: When stages_csv is empty (parser bug or direct call) but _CYCLE_MAX_ITER is set, _cycle_load_template silently sets _CYCLE_STAGES=() with no error and no cycle.config.invalid event; the loop then runs each iteration and dispatches zero members, returning rc=0 as if the cycle converged — the old code emitted reason=no_stages and returned 1.

The *) defense-in-depth branch in _cycle_eval_one_condition, _cycle_check_until, and _cycle_check_abort_when calls error() (stderr only) but emits no _cycle_emit event, so an unrecognized op reaching an evaluator at runtime is invisible to the structured event stream and any alerting on events.jsonl.

findings.category: observability — missing structured event at validation
findings.message: The abort_when.op and until.op invalid-op error paths in _tpl_validate_cycles emit only to stderr via error() with no structured event; this is consistent with other _tpl_validate_* functions but means op-validation failures are not observable in the event log.

The matches case uses [[ "$actual" =~ $expected ]] with $expected unquoted; an invalid ERE pattern (e.g., an unmatched bracket) causes [[ ]] to exit with rc=2 rather than rc=1, which the evaluator silently treats as no-match without logging a diagnostic.

findings.category: SLO impact — breaking change for ne op
findings.message: The multi-condition exit_when validator now accepts only neq and rejects ne, but the evaluators still accept ne|neq at runtime; any existing template using op: ne in a multi-condition exit_when will hard-fail at load after this change with no migration path or deprecation warning.

findings.category: SLO impact — load-time hard failure for previously-silenced invalid ops
findings.message: Templates that previously had invalid ops in abort_when silently ran to max_iterations; after this change they hard-fail at load, which is the desired behavior but increases blast radius on upgrade for any template with a typo op.

findings.category: partial validation — empty op passes guard
findings.message: The until.op validation in _tpl_validate_cycles is guarded by if [[ -n "$uo" ]]; an absent op passes the op-specific check silently, though _cycle_load_template will subsequently catch it as an incomplete until block with a less precise error message.

The numeric guard ^-?[0-9]+$ accepts leading zeros (e.g., 010), which bash arithmetic treats as decimal 10, not octal 10; this is not a crash risk but could confuse template authors who expect octal semantics.

reason: the sre lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
